compile: revert the startup check of every module graph offset (#46461)

### What does this PR do?

Reverts the check from #46021 that validates every offset in a `bun
build --compile` executable's module graph at startup.

`StandaloneModuleGraph::from_bytes` goes back to how it read the graph
before #46021:

- `slice_to`, `slice_to_mut` and `slice_to_z` trust the `StringPointer`s
that `to_bytes` wrote. They `debug_assert!` the bounds instead of
returning an error.
- `slice_to_z` no longer reads the byte after each string to check for
the NUL. For `contents`, that read touched a page at the end of every
embedded file before the program started.
- The `Corruption` enum, `RecordChain` and `checked_range` are removed.
The optional records after the module table use the same bounds checks
they had before #46021.
- The name lookup in `LazySourceMap::load` is reverted too, because it
used the same helpers.

After this PR, an executable whose graph fields were overwritten can
crash at startup again instead of printing `Corrupted module graph:
<field> is out of range`.

#### Not reverted

These changes from #46021 are in the same file but aren't part of that
check:

- **ELF payload checks:** the payload address and length are still
checked against the mapped segment.
- **Truncated executables on Linux:** they still exit with the "is
truncated" error. This happens once per process, not once per module.
- **Entry point ID:** the check existed before #46021, which only fixed
an off-by-one (`>` on the record count became `>=` on the module count).
The fix stays, under the old error variant, because `entry_point()`
would otherwise panic on an index that is out of bounds.
- **`to_bytes`:** it still counts file names that aren't valid UTF-8
correctly.
- **`bun build --compile` errors:** the error for a cache directory path
that is too long, and the fix for an `--outfile` name that is too long.

### How did you verify your code works?

`git diff 9b4284f7^ -- src/standalone_graph` now shows only the changes
listed under "Not reverted".

In `test/bundler/compile-corrupted-embed.test.ts`, the test that
overwrote six graph fields now covers only the entry point ID. The tests
for a bad length, a bad address and a truncated file are unchanged.

Debug build on Linux x64:

| Test file | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test/bundler/compile-corrupted-embed.test.ts` | 3 pass |
| `test/bundler/compile-asset-bunfs.test.ts` | 10 pass |
| `test/bundler/bundler_compile_prelinked.test.ts` | 81 pass |

I didn't measure startup time before and after.

Addresses the open OpenSSF Scorecard code scanning alerts #716, #693, #694, #477 (pip not pinned by hash) and #23 (GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7).

## Pip installs pinned by hash

| Workflow | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ubuntu.yml` (ci_meson_install) | `pip install meson` (unpinned) | `--require-hashes -r .github/requirements/meson.txt` (meson 1.12.1) |
| `semgrep.yml` | `semgrep==1.168.0` (no hash) | `--require-hashes -r .github/requirements/semgrep.txt` |
| `check_amalgamation.yml` | astyle and jinja2 `requirements.txt` without hashes | `--require-hashes` with hashed files |

- The hashed `requirements.txt` files are compiled from `requirements.in` with `pip-compile --generate-hashes` (pip-tools 7.6.2, Python 3.14, the Python of ubuntu-26.04), so Dependabot can recompile them. `.github/requirements` is added to `dependabot.yml`. The astyle comment and the Dependabot ignore rule are unchanged; the comment now lives in `tools/astyle/requirements.in`.
- `check_amalgamation.yml` now installs the natvis requirements from the PR tree (`$MAIN_DIR`), as it already does for astyle. Otherwise this PR's own run would apply `--require-hashes` to develop's unhashed file. The natvis tool itself still runs from develop.
- `make amalgamate` and `make natvis` keep working: pip switches to hash-checking mode by itself when the file contains hashes.

## KaTeX and DOMPurify (Mermaid checker)

- Mermaid 11.17.2 (the newest 11.x release) still requires `katex ^0.16.47`, and Dependabot keeps the checker on Mermaid 11 to match Material for MkDocs. The fix (GHSA-238p-pmpm-9mq7, fixed in 0.18.2) therefore needs an npm `overrides` entry: `katex` 0.18.11.
- `npm audit` then also reported DOMPurify 3.4.16 (GHSA-cg2g-xh64-v4q7, GHSA-mrv2-3pqr-j5jr, GHSA-c6gr-qvv4-5v3f). The lockfile now has 3.4.17, which is within Mermaid's `^3.3.3` range.
- `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities. `node scripts/mermaid/check_mermaid.mjs docs`: 26 diagrams checked, 0 invalid.

## Verification

- All four hashed files install with `--require-hashes` in `python:3.14` (Semgrep reports 1.168.0).
- `reuse lint` is compliant, and the workflow YAML parses.

## Breaking changes

None. This only touches CI and tooling; the library and its public API are unchanged.

title: Let replicas resync while FAILOVER waits for the target to catch up
body:
`FAILOVER` without `TIMEOUT` never finishes if the target's replication link drops while the master is in `waiting-for-sync`. Client writes on the master stay paused until an operator runs `FAILOVER ABORT`.

The master waits for the target to ack the full stream (`updateFailoverStatus()`). But `syncCommand()` (`replication.c:1240-1243`) refuses every (P)SYNC with `-NOMASTERLINK Can't SYNC while failing over` whenever `failover_state != NO_FAILOVER`, and that includes the reconnect of the very target it waits for. The replica treats `-NOMASTERLINK` as transient and retries forever. With `TIMEOUT` the failover aborts at the deadline; with `TIMEOUT` and `FORCE` it fails over to a target that couldn't catch up, losing the writes it missed. Any non-target replica whose link drops during the wait is also locked out until the failover ends.

#### Repro

A master, B replica.

1. `kill -STOP B`, then `SET k2 v2` on A, so B's ack lags.
2. `FAILOVER TO B` (no timeout).
3. `CLIENT KILL TYPE replica` on A, standing in for a network glitch or `repl-timeout`.
4. `kill -CONT B`.

On `f12f2a1`, for 60 s:
- A reports `master_failover_state:waiting-for-sync` and `connected_slaves:0`.
- B has `master_link_status:down` and logged `-NOMASTERLINK Can't SYNC while failing over` 51 times.
- `SET k3` on A blocks.

Only `FAILOVER ABORT` releases it.

#### Fix

Refuse (P)SYNC only in `FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS`.

- **Why WAIT_FOR_SYNC is safe.** In `FAILOVER_WAIT_FOR_SYNC` the node is still an ordinary master with client writes paused. Serving a partial or full resync there doesn't propagate anything; only replicationCron PINGs, which already flow in that state without TIMEOUT. It doesn't change the node's replication ID or offset (except the pre-existing first-replica-with-no-backlog case). It is the same as serving a replica while `CLIENT PAUSE WRITE` is active.
- **FAILOVER_IN_PROGRESS is unchanged.** The node is a replica of the target by then, and the check below it (`masterhost && repl_state != CONNECTED`) would refuse anyway.

#### Tests

`failover target can resync while the master waits for it to catch up` (`tests/integration/failover.tcl`):
- The target is `SIGSTOP`ped and a write is made on the master.
- `FAILOVER TO target` (no timeout), then `CLIENT KILL TYPE replica` on the master, then the target is resumed.
- The failover must complete with only partial resyncs (`sync_full` unchanged), and the digests must match.

Negative control (unfixed `f12f2a1`, test file only):
```
[err]: failover target can resync while the master waits for it to catch up
Failover from node 0 to node 1 did not finish
   node 1 and node 2 logs: "-NOMASTERLINK Can't SYNC while failing over" x12 / x11
```

With the fix it passes (17/17 in the file), and it passed 3 more runs.

Suites run with the fix: the same 17 files as PR 1, 778 tests, 0 failures.

`repro_f3_failover_stuck.sh` against the fixed build:
- 0 `-NOMASTERLINK` refusals.
- A logs `Partial resynchronization request from 127.0.0.1:7202 accepted` during `waiting-for-sync`, then `Failover target ... is synced, failing over`, and B is promoted about 0.3 s after the link drop. A write on A now gets `READONLY` (A is a replica) instead of blocking.

TLA+ check of the change: a scratch copy of `Psync2.tla` with `Bug = "fofix3"` refuses syncs only when `fo[m] = "INPROG"`, on top of the F2 fix.
- Liveness `FailoverWaitEnds` now holds: 2,140 distinct states. The same copy with `Bug = "fofix"` still reports the violation.
- Safety still holds, including `AtMostOneMaster`: `Psync2_failover_fix` at 2,000,346 distinct states and `Psync2_mixed` at 10,535,704.
- The liveness bounds are small (one FAILOVER, one fault, no FORCE).

#### Open design question (for reviewers)

The refusal has been there since FAILOVER was introduced (#8315), with the comment "Don't let replicas sync with us while we're failing over". The PR discussion doesn't seem to motivate it for the waiting phase. Alternatives:
- (a) this PR: allow every replica during WAIT_FOR_SYNC.
- (b) allow only the designated target, matched like `findReplica()` by announced ip and listening port, or every replica when no target was given.
- (c) instead abort WAIT_FOR_SYNC when the target disconnects.

(a) is the smallest change and also unblocks non-target replicas; (b) keeps the replica set frozen at the cost of about 15 lines. I don't see a correctness argument for (b). A full sync started during the wait forks a BGSAVE, which the later `replicationSetMaster()` / new-master sync already handles like any REPLICAOF transition. If maintainers prefer, the issue text at the end of this file can be filed instead of the PR.

Note: this PR and #15851 both add a test at the end of `tests/integration/failover.tcl`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. Checked together on a temporary branch: 19/19 tests in the file pass.

> **Overview**
> **Fixes stuck `FAILOVER` when the target’s replication link drops during `waiting-for-sync`.** Previously `syncCommand()` rejected all (P)SYNC with `-NOMASTERLINK` for any non-`NO_FAILOVER` state, so the designated target could not reconnect and the master would wait forever with writes paused.

title: Set a read timeout on the Gateway API conformance entry points
body:
### What does this PR do?

Sets a 1s `respondingTimeouts.readTimeout` on the Gateway API conformance entry points, as the TCP entry points already do on `master`.

### Motivation

A TLS connection matching no route is terminated and handed to the HTTPS forwarder, which waits for an HTTP request the conformance TCP client never sends. The connection is only released at the entry point read timeout, which defaults to 60s and therefore outlives the conformance consistency window: the client blocks on its first attempt instead of retrying, and the test fails.

The window where an entry point carries no TCP route is short, but a configuration transition opens it, for instance when the previous test removes the last TLS listener. This is what makes `TLSRouteMixedTerminationSameNamespace` flaky.

This only changes the conformance fixture. The underlying behaviour, an unroutable TLS connection being parked on the HTTP server instead of being closed, is untouched.

- ~[ ] Added/updated documentation~

The same change is already on `master`, carried by the v3.7 into master merge-back.

title: Harden `/settings` redirect to prevent open redirect via referrer
body:
This change addresses the flagged code-scanning issue in the web app’s settings flow: redirecting to a user-controlled referrer could allow open redirects. The update constrains post-save navigation to same-host HTTP(S) referrers and safely falls back to the index page.

- **Security fix: constrain referrer-based redirect**
  - Updated `settings_update()` in `maigret/web/app.py` to parse and validate `request.referrer` before redirecting.
  - Redirect now proceeds only when:
    - scheme is `http` or `https`
    - referrer host matches `request.host`
  - Otherwise, it redirects to `url_for("index")`.

- **Minimal code changes**
  - Added `from urllib.parse import urlparse`.
  - Replaced direct `redirect(request.referrer or url_for('index'))` with validated logic.

```python
referrer = (request.referrer or '').replace('\\', '/')
parsed_referrer = urlparse(referrer)
if (
    parsed_referrer.scheme in ('http', 'https')
    and parsed_referrer.netloc == request.host
):
    return redirect(referrer)
return redirect(url_for('index'))
```

**1. `batch/batch-prompt.md` never asks the worker to archive the JD** *(fixed by the linked PR)*

The report template has `**URL:**` and then `## Machine Summary`, but no `## Job Description (archived verbatim)` section. `AGENTS.md` rule #2789 makes that section **REQUIRED** ("JD archival is REQUIRED, not optional"), and `check-jd-archive.mjs` is wired into `test-all.mjs`. ```

title: Prevent agent context usage from appearing under another conversation
body:
### What this PR does

Before this PR: The renderer trusted the context-usage cache key without checking that the cached reading belonged to the selected session.

After this PR:
- Cache publications include their owning session ID.
- The renderer displays a reading only when its session ID matches the selected session.

```ts
const sessionUsage =
  sessionId && cachedUsage?.sessionId === sessionId ? cachedUsage : null
```

### Why we need it and why it was done in this way

A misrouted cache value could show one agent conversation’s context usage under another. Checking ownership at the renderer boundary fails closed without discarding valid readings retained across reconnects.

The following tradeoffs were made:

- Mismatched readings are hidden until a correctly owned reading is available.

The following alternatives were considered:

- Clearing readings when a session closes would discard valid usage retained for reconnects.

title: fix(trie-router): keep first value for duplicate path params
body:
### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code
- [ ] Add [TSDoc](https://tsdoc.org/)/[JSDoc](https://jsdoc.app/about-getting-started) to document the code

## Summary

Fixes #5422.

`TrieRouter` did not consistently keep the **first** value when the same path parameter name appeared more than once (e.g. `/:id/:id/x`). `RegExpRouter` / `LinearRouter` already follow first-wins, and `src/router/common.case.test.ts` asserts that for `/:id/:id`. For longer paths the trie overwrite left a different value, so `SmartRouter` could change `c.req.param('id')` merely by registering an unrelated route that switches the selected router.

### Root cause

In `src/router/trie-router/node.ts`, `search()` assigned `params[name] = part` (and the regexp-matcher equivalent), overwriting earlier values for the same name. That made `/:id/:id/x` return the second segment and `/:id/:id/:id` return the middle one.

### Fix

Record a path param only if that name is not already an own property (`Object.hasOwn`). Nullish assignment (`??=`) alone is not enough because a normal `{}` already has `constructor` on the prototype (caught by the reserved-words suite).

Tests extended in shared router cases, TrieRouter node tests, and a SmartRouter/`Hono` integration case that matches the issue reproduction.

## AI disclosure

Assisted by AI tooling; changes and tests were reviewed and verified against the failing reproduction from #5422.

message:
Skip unchanged children when slicing in the differ (#59242)

Summary:
> This touches the differ, so I'm happy to split it if that's easier to review: (1) a refactor that moves the per-child logic of `sliceChildShadowNodeViewPairs` into helpers, with no behavior change, and (2) the change below, behind the new feature flag.

When a node changes, the differ (`calculateShadowViewMutations`, `ReactCommon/react/renderer/mounting/Differentiator.cpp`) slices the children of its old and new revision with `sliceChildShadowNodeViewPairs` and compares the two lists. A commit clones only the path from the changed node to the root, so most of those children are the same `ShadowNode` in both revisions.

**Current behavior.** Slicing builds a `ShadowViewNodePair`, including a `ShadowView`, for every child in both lists, recursing into flattened children, before the comparison finds that a child is unchanged and skips it. While a list scrolls, the ScrollView writes its content offset into its state on every frame, so every frame produces a commit that changes one node deep in the tree, and the differ slices every sibling along the path to it, twice. In the RNTester chat scenario below, 36 of the 56 child pairs compared in such a diff are the same node in both revisions.

**With this change.** Behind the new `skipUnchangedChildrenInDifferentiator` feature flag (default `false`), the differ slices the children of a matched pair side by side with the new `sliceChangedChildShadowNodeViewPairs` and leaves out each child that is the same node in both revisions at the same offset. Such a child and its flattened descendants give equal pairs in both lists, which the differ matches without a mutation, so the mutations computed from the shorter lists are the same. A child is kept when its offset differs, because a flattened ancestor moved and its frame has to be updated. The side-by-side slicing gives up, and the differ slices both revisions in full as before, when the revisions differ in a way that could change the order or the kind of the pairs: child count, tags, flattening, position type, order index (`zIndex`), visibility or `ChildrenFormStackingContext`, or when view culling is enabled.

The per-child logic of the existing slicer moves into helpers that both slicers share, so they can't drift apart.

## Changelog:

[Internal]

Pull Request resolved: https://github.com/react/react-native/pull/59242

Test Plan:
- `clang-format --dry-run --Werror` on the changed C++ files passes. `yarn featureflags` regenerated the accessors.
- **Fantom.** `Mounting-itest.js` now runs with `fantom_flags skipUnchangedChildrenInDifferentiator:*`, so every existing differ test also runs with the flag on, and it adds tests for an unchanged child next to a changed one, an unchanged child of a flattened view that moves, a scrolled ScrollView with unchanged siblings, a child added next to unchanged children and a child whose `zIndex` changes. `yarn fantom Mounting-itest`: 56 passed (14 tests × 4 flag combinations). The full suite (`FANTOM_FORCE_CI_MODE=1 yarn fantom`) passes with the flag's default switched to `true` locally, so that every test runs with it on (3,325 passed, 108 skipped), and with it off (same counts), twice each. In a first run with the flag on, the tester crashed once in `setUpDefaultReactNativeEnvironment-Globals-ResizeObserver-itest.js`; it did not crash again in three runs of that file alone or in two more full runs.
- **Same mutations on device.** With a local checker that ran the differ twice for every commit, with and without the side-by-side slicing, and compared the full mutation lists, about 7,500 commits in RNTester on a physical iPhone produced no difference: mounting and unmounting 1000 views, re-rendering, a reflow that moves siblings, opacity animation, list item updates, `removeClippedSubviews`, `adjustsFontSizeToFit` text updates, scrolling a chat FlatList, typing in a TextInput, FlatList and SectionList scrolling.
- Android was not built or tested. The slicing is shared C++, and the Android-specific branches (`useTraitHiddenOnAndroid`) are mirrored from the existing slicer.
- **Measurement.** RNTester built with `xcodebuild` in Release and run on a physical iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 26.6.1). The two arms are the same binary with the flag switched by a launch argument, in the order before, after, after, before. Scrolling was driven by [Argent](https://github.com/software-mansion/argent) on the physical iPhone. Timed: the diff phase of each mount transaction from `TransactionTelemetry`, on the main thread.

| RNTester Playground, a FlatList of 500 multi-line messages, 20 flings down and 20 up per launch (~8,800 transactions) | before | this PR | change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| diff time per launch | 1,102 ms | 518 ms | −53.4% |
| diff time per transaction | 126.1 µs | 58.8 µs | −53.4% |
| diff time per 1–2-mutation transaction (the per-frame scroll updates) | 107.2 µs | 44.5 µs | −58.4% |

| RNTester Playground, 1000 labels mounted and unmounted, 10 times per arm | before | this PR | change |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| diff time per mount or unmount (median) | 2.54 ms | 2.45 ms | within noise |

A mount gains nothing, since every node is new; the second table shows that giving up on the side-by-side slicing costs nothing measurable.

opencode: migrate plugin to the V2 plugin API

The OpenCode plugin does not load on OpenCode 2.x. Three separate V1
constructs were rejected or removed:

- The default export was a bare `async () => ({...})`. V2 requires a
  definition object with an `id` and an `effect`/`setup` function, and
  fails the load with:

      Plugin must export a default definition with an id and an effect or
      setup function. (cause: SchemaError(Expected object at ["default"]))

- The `config` mutation hook no longer exists. Skill and command
  registration move to `ctx.skill.transform` and `ctx.command.transform`.

- `experimental.chat.system.transform` no longer exists. System-prompt
  edits move to `ctx.session.hook("context", ...)`.

`Skill.Info` also requires `path`, not the `location` shown in the V2
plugin docs; registering with `location` disabled the whole plugin with
`SchemaError(Missing key at ["path"])`.

The V1 plugin also registered commands with `agent`, `model`, and
`subagent`. `Command.Info` in V2 carries only `name` and `description`,
so those fields are dropped; the command file remains the source of truth
for the prompt body and description.

The driver and tests move to the V2 registration API. Three tests that
asserted V1-only behaviour are removed: preserving a user-defined
command, idempotent skill-path registration, and command metadata
passthrough. None is expressible through the V2 command editor, which
exposes only `add`.

INSTALL.md now documents the install that works on 2.0.18 without a
plugin (global `skills/` plus `commands/`, both discovered natively), and
keeps the plugin as the always-on option. `opencode.json` uses the plural
`plugins` field.

title: feat(session-ui): move user message actions into a chevron menu on each bubble
body:
Back-to-back user messages already group into a run, but each message's actions sat beside the bubble and collided with its text (the Revert and ⋯ icons drew over the first words of the bubble, and stayed stuck after a menu closed). This moves every user message's actions into a chevron menu inside its own bubble and tidies the run's meta line and pending steers around it.

### Changes

**All user messages**
- A chevron (`chevron-down`, 20px ghost IconButton, no tooltip) sits in the bubble's top trailing corner, centred on the first line and inset the same distance from the top and the side. It shows only while that bubble is hovered or keyboard-focused.
- The menu is the shared `Menu` (`bg-layer-01`), opens upward 4px from the chevron with its trailing edge on the chevron's, and flips down when there is no room.
- Menu: the send time as a relative header (Today, Yesterday, the date, then the date with its year), Copy message, Fork from here, and a divider before Revert to here. The newest delivered prompt says **Undo** with the undo icon instead.
- English copy: "Rewind to here" → "Revert to here", and the toast "Rewound" → "Reverted". A new `ui.message.undoMessage` key ("Undo").
- The meta line (agent · model) shows and hides with the chevron, and no longer stays visible after a menu closes: a closed menu returns focus without a ring, so only keyboard focus keeps the chevron and meta line shown.
- New prompts arriving in a busy session fade in as their row opens, instead of being revealed by the row's edge.

**Runs**
- The run's bubbles and the 4px gaps between them are one hover zone: anywhere in it shows the run's meta line under the last bubble, with no flash between bubbles, and an open menu keeps it. The space beside a bubble and the meta line itself do not count.
- A steer delivered into the run above slides into place: the gaps and meta lines it moves now spring together, so the bubble below holds still instead of jumping up and back down. Arrivals still snap, since the arriving row grows in.

**Pending steers**
- The meta line reads `agent · model · Pending`. Pending stays in view; the agent and model show on hover like any other message. A waiting steer now always names its agent and model, so the "only what it changes" previous-selection index is removed.
- Move to queue (list icon), Copy message and Delete (in the menu's critical style, after a divider) live in the chevron menu; the inline ↓ and 🗑 are gone. Fork is hidden while a steer is pending.
- A steer that starts a pending run shows its Pending line once it has settled; one that joins a pending run carries the run's line down as it grows in.

### Testing
- `bun typecheck` in `packages/session-ui`, `packages/ui`, `packages/app`; `typecheck:e2e` shows only the errors already on `dev`.
- `bun run lint:changed` is clean.
- Component tests: the full `packages/session-ui` suite (180 passed), with new cases for the chevron position, the menu's placement, the run hover zone including the gaps, Undo on the newest prompt, and the pending meta line.
- App e2e, run locally: `session-header` revert/Undo, `session-queue`, `timeline-geometry`, `timeline-stream` (quote keyboard), `session-timeline-accessibility`. `btw-sidebar`'s owner-warning assertion fails locally on `dev` as well; the rest of that test passes.

message:
security-guidance: do not review against a baseline from another checkout

The turn baseline (stash SHA, HEAD, untracked snapshot) is kept per
session, and the Stop review used it in whatever checkout the turn ended
in. After the session entered another worktree, that worktree's older
commits looked like commits made this turn and its files were diffed
against the first checkout's, so code committed long before was reviewed
and reported again (anthropics/claude-code#102567).

The prompt hook now stores the repo root and the prompt time beside the
baseline. When the Stop review runs in a different checkout it leaves the
baseline out and uses what that checkout can say for itself: its own HEAD
when the turn began (from its reflog) for the commit range, HEAD for file
contents, and file times to leave out uncommitted files last written
before the turn. A baseline taken after a finding records the checkout it
was taken in.

A prompt in a folder that is not a repo no longer replaces the untracked
snapshot of the kept baseline with an empty one, which made every
untracked file in the repo look new at the next Stop.

Stop rows carry `bl_origin`: 0 same checkout, 1 another worktree, 2
another repository, 3 a folder that is gone, 4 no baseline; plus 10 or 20
when the baseline is an earlier turn's.

_Requested by **Samuel Attard** · [Slack thread](https://electronhq.slack.com/archives/C0BERTA8EKW/p1792809012885369)_

The install-build-tools action copies `C:\Python311\python.exe` to `python3.exe`, so every Windows build depends on the runner image installing Python 3.11 at that exact path. The image is moving to Python 3.14 (electron/infra#427), and 3.11 hasn't had a Windows installer with security fixes since April 2024. With this change the step only creates `python3.exe` when `python3` doesn't already run. It takes the directory from the Python 3 on PATH (via `sys.executable`), so it works on both the current 3.11 image and the new 3.14 one, which ships its own `python3.exe`. The infra PR adds a temporary `C:\Python311` junction so release branches keep building until this is backported to 42-x-y through 46-x-y.

title: fix(plugins): run ralph-wiggum and output-style .sh hooks through bash with a quoted path
body:
Refs #95673. Also fixes the ralph-wiggum / output-style half of #78490.

## What changes

Three bundled plugins registered their hook as a bare, unquoted script path:

| plugin | event | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ralph-wiggum` | `Stop` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh` | `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh"` |
| `learning-output-style` | `SessionStart` | `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh` | `bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh"` |
| `explanatory-output-style` | `SessionStart` | same | same |

This is the form `security-guidance` already uses (`bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/sg-python.sh" …`). Each plugin's `version` goes 1.0.0 → 1.0.1 in `plugin.json` and in the `marketplace.json` entry, because the updater compares the `plugin.json` version: without the bump, existing installs stay on the cached 1.0.0 copy and never receive the new `hooks.json`.

## Why

Shell-form hook commands are handed to a shell (`sh -c` on macOS/Linux, Git Bash on Windows) with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` exported, and the shell expands the variable. Three consequences of the bare form:

1. **Spaces in the plugin root break the hook on every platform.** Unquoted, the expansion word-splits, the shell tries to execute the first fragment, and the hook exits 127 with `not found`. For these three hooks that is silent: the output styles contribute no context and the ralph loop never continues. (#78490; a home directory like `C:\Users\Jane Doe` or `/Users/jane doe` is enough.)
2. **The bare form depends on the script's exec bit.** A delivery path that drops `+x` turns the hook into `Permission denied` (exit 126). `bash "<path>"` reads the script as data and does not care.
3. **On Windows the bare form leans on the CLI.** Current Claude Code prepends `bash ` to a hook command whose first word is a `.sh` file when it runs hooks through Git Bash (see the 2.1.161 changelog entry for #63828), so on an up‑to‑date CLI with Git Bash detected these hooks already get an interpreter — but still unquoted, so point 1 applies, and hosts on older CLIs get the file-association behaviour #95673 describes. Naming the interpreter in the plugin removes the dependency either way; the CLI leaves a command that already starts with `bash` untouched.

## What could break, and for whom

- macOS/Linux/Windows-with-Git-Bash users of these plugins whose plugin root has no space: no behaviour change; the same script runs under the same bash (`stop-hook.sh` is `#!/bin/bash`, the session-start handlers are `#!/usr/bin/env bash`).
- Users whose plugin root contains a space: the hooks start working after they update to 1.0.1.
- Windows without Git Bash (hooks default to PowerShell): these bash scripts could not run before and still cannot; the failure stays a non-blocking hook error.
- Rollback: revert this commit; nothing else reads these versions.

## Considered and deliberately not done

- **Exec form** (`"command": "bash", "args": ["${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…"]`) avoids quoting entirely, but on Windows a bare `bash` spawned without a shell can resolve to WSL's `bash.exe` rather than Git Bash, and exec form needs a newer CLI than shell form. Shell form with quotes matches the existing convention.
- **`"shell": "bash"` on each hook** would turn the no-Git-Bash Windows case into an explicit "requires bash" error. Left out to keep parity with `security-guidance`; happy to add if preferred.
- **hookify's unquoted `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/…`** has the same word-splitting problem (and blocks every tool call when it hits). It already has two open PRs, #79644 and #81670, which also quote the three files here but keep the bare-path form; this PR supersedes their hunks for these three files only.
- **`/ralph-loop`'s `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/setup-ralph-loop.sh"`** runs through the Bash tool, is already quoted, and is the subject of #80495; not touched.
- `ralph-wiggum`'s `stop-hook.sh` needs `jq`, which Git for Windows does not ship, so on Windows the Stop hook now launches correctly but still fails at `jq` when a loop is active. Separate problem; noted as a follow-up.
- The reporter's two follow-ups — a CI check that every bundled `hooks.json` command names an interpreter, and a plugin-docs note — are not in this PR. The hooks reference already says shell-form commands run through Git Bash on Windows; the lint is a reasonable follow-up and would be the regression guard this repo currently lacks for `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`.

## Verification

- All seven edited JSON files parse; `claude plugin validate` passes on the marketplace root and on each of the three plugins (the only warning is the pre-existing `security-guidance` entry/plugin.json version mismatch).
- Reproduced the failure and the fix the way the CLI runs shell-form hooks, with the plugins copied under a directory named `plugin root with space`:
  - before: `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=".../plugin root with space/ralph-wiggum" sh -c '${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh'` → exit 127, `sh: 1: .../plugin: not found` (same for both session-start hooks)
  - after: `sh -c 'bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh"'` → exit 0; the session-start hooks emit valid `hookSpecificOutput` JSON (1018 and 3034 chars of `additionalContext`); with an active `.claude/ralph-loop.local.md` the Stop hook reads stdin and returns `{"decision":"block",…,"🔄 Ralph iteration 2 …"}`.
  - after, with `chmod -x stop-hook.sh`: still exit 0; the quoted-but-bare form from #79644/#81670 gives exit 126 `Permission denied` in that case.
- End to end with a real CLI (2.1.280-dev, Linux), loading each modified plugin with `--plugin-dir` from the spaced path in `-p` mode: the debug log shows `Hook SessionStart (bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks-handlers/session-start.sh") provided additionalContext (1018 chars)` and the model echoed the explanatory instructions; the unmodified copy logged `Hook SessionStart:startup (SessionStart) error: /bin/sh: 1: .../main: not found` and the model answered `NONE`. With ralph-wiggum and an active loop file, the log shows `Hook Stop (bash "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/stop-hook.sh") returned permissionDecision: deny` and the loop advanced to iteration 2.
- Not checked on a Windows machine (none available here). The Windows claim rests on the CLI behaviour described above plus the reporter's own before/after in #95673.
- `plugins/plugin-dev/.../validate-hook-schema.sh` was tried and fails identically on `main` and on this branch (`jq: Cannot index string with number` — it does not understand the plugin wrapper format, #90292), so it is not a usable check here.
- This repo has no test harness for `plugins/*/hooks/hooks.json`, so there is no automated regression test in the diff; the interpreter-prefix lint above would be it.

<!-- NO CHANGELOG: bundled plugin content, not a CLI release note -->

body:
### The author should do the following, if applicable

- [x] Add tests
- [x] Run tests
- [x] `bun run format:fix && bun run lint:fix` to format the code

## Summary

Fixes #5403

In `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts`, `defaultIsContentTypeBinary()` matches `(?:/|\+)(?:json|xml)\s*(?:;|$)`, which matches content types ending in `+xml` like `application/vnd.apple.installer+xml` and `application/vnd.mozilla.xul+xml`.
These media types are binary archives (Apple installer xar packages, Mozilla XUL archives), but were being treated as text and decoded with `res.text()` as UTF-8, corrupting binary bytes into `\uFFFD`.

## Changes

- In `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.ts`: added `BINARY_XML_ARCHIVE_CONTENT_TYPES` regex to explicitly detect binary `+xml` archive formats before the text content-type check.
- In `src/adapter/aws-lambda/handler.test.ts`: added unit test coverage verifying `application/vnd.apple.installer+xml` is treated as binary and base64-encoded.

AsyncAuthedProvider.create_async_generator did not invalidate the stale
credentials. The persisted auth cache file was left in place (its deletion
was commented out) and the in-memory class state (_api_key, _headers,
_cookies, _expires, request_config) was not cleared. Because a rejected
token can still look valid by its local expiry claim, login_generator
reused the stale token/cookies/headers, so the retried request failed
again and the second MissingAuthError propagated to the caller - leaving
the stale auth_OpenaiChat.json behind and forcing users to delete it
manually and restart.

Add a reset_auth() hook to AsyncAuthedProvider (deletes the cache file)
and call it in the auth-failure except block before re-logging in.
OpenaiChat overrides reset_auth() to also clear its cached class state and
reset request_config, so the re-login performs a fully fresh authentication
- automating the manual workaround from the issue.

Adds unit tests in etc/unittest/test_auth_retry.py covering stale-cache
invalidation, cache-file deletion, missing-cache login and persistent
failure propagation.

body: Fixes #3827 ## Bug In production builds `invariant()` is a no-op, so `easingDefinitionToFunction` returns `undefined` for an unrecognised easing string. ## What changed

`search` now matches saved facts the way the facts keyword index does, and a newer correction comes back ahead of the fact it corrects. Found through harness case cr-05: a channel post was corrected in another channel, and `search` returned four pages and no saved fact, so every harness answered with the retracted figure.

**Saved-fact matching (a plain fix, no flag).** `retrieval.saved_facts`, returned beside `search` and `query` rows, kept a fact only when its text contained three quarters of the query's words as raw lowercase substrings, so "renewal" never matched "renews" and "count" matched inside "countersigned". Now:
- Words match whole after stemming with the brain's full-text language, through the facts keyword index's own expression, and the scan uses `idx_facts_fts`. Words of a CJK script still match as substrings (`LIKE ANY`).
- The threshold is still three quarters of the query's words (both words of a two-word query), but never more than four, so a question sent verbatim can still find the short fact that answers it.
- Words that frame a question about a figure (count, number, total, amount) count toward neither side.
- Ordering (most matched words, then newest) and the five-fact cap are unchanged.

**`search.saved_facts_supersede` (new, default on; `false`, `off`, `0` or `no` turns it off).** A newer fact with a correction cue ("correction", "ignore the 52", "disregard", "not what I posted") that shares two matched words with a returned fact comes back too, even below the threshold, and ranks ahead of it. The older fact carries `corrected_by`, also shown in the MCP text reply. A correction only counts when it is about the same thing: not saved under another entity, not of lower trust, sharing a name the older fact matched, and either adding a figure or withdrawing what was said. So an acknowledgement ("thanks for the correction, noted") or a reply reporting a correction made elsewhere corrects nothing. Nothing stored changes.

**Moved.** The matcher moves to `src/core/search/saved-facts-match.ts`, which keeps `ops/search.ts` under its size cap. An entity-resolved search keeps the `corrected_by` label on the entity copy of a fact. A `BEHAVIOR_CHANGES` row (`saved_facts_stems`, `since: '0.60.493.0'`) names the off switch.

`search` still never runs the `query` facts arm, facts block or temporal reserve; the facts-arm row-cap starvation is #7743.

## Why

In the keyless HARN-1 replay (816 harness `search` calls across 443 trials, each run against the facts its trial had ingested by then), the author's correction ranked above the retracted post in 27 of 27 cr-05 reads, against 1 of 27 on master. cr-08 returned the earlier correction on 30 of 32 reads (27 of 32 on master). No read lost a non-assistant fact master returns, and no `corrected_by` label fell outside the corrections cases. Measured on e9f1288a6; later commits change only the scan's index use, a regex form and docs.

On a synthetic fixture of 400 facts (10 placeholder entities by 6 attributes, 130 queries), measured before the review fixes, master returned 320 facts (287 relevant, 90%) and this PR 403 (370 relevant, 92%), flag on or off; the fixture holds no corrections.

## Blast radius

Every `search` and `query` reply that carries `retrieval.saved_facts`, over the CLI and MCP. Remote callers stay inside the facts read policy: a private correction is never returned and never relabels a returned fact (tested as a remote caller). The scan stays on `idx_facts_fts` unless a query word is CJK (EXPLAIN test on 20,000 facts).

Past it come the PR's base from `gh pr view`, then the remote's live default branch from `git ls-remote --symref`, then `origin/main`, then `origin/master`. A repository whose default is `develop` or `trunk` keeps it. When nothing resolves, the command fails closed with a named line. `resolveBaseBranch`, gate-diff's `defaultBase` and `gstack-diff-scope` all use it. - **Base-relative steps refuse a base that contains HEAD** (`BASE_CONTAINS_HEAD`, docs/troubleshooting.md#base-contains-head): ship-queue receipt binding (`bindShippedReceipt`), `gstack-review-plan`, the pregate context and `sealed`, `gstack-gate-diff`, `gstack-diff-scope` and `gstack-docs-candidate snapshot`. ## Why

`MemoryRunStore.put` accepts replacement snapshots for an existing run ID, including an updated thread ID, just like the SQL repository. Its old thread-index entry remained behind: the original thread could still list and count the reassigned run, and `delete_by_thread(old_thread)` deleted the current row belonging to the new thread. fix(coding-agent): name the package manager in pi update only when it owns the install (#11628)

Fixes #7756.

Problem: `detectInstallMethod()` classifies any path containing `/pnpm/`
as pnpm. An install that only lives under `PNPM_HOME`, for example a
wrapper under `$PNPM_HOME/global-nub/5/node_modules/...`, is detected as
pnpm. `pi update` then correctly refuses to self-update (the path is not
under `pnpm root -g`), but `getSelfUpdateUnavailableInstruction()`
printed:

```
This installation is not managed by a global pnpm install. Update it with the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides it.
```

Fix: name the package manager only when it owns the install (managed but
not writable). All other cases fall through to the neutral message:

```
Update @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent using the package manager, wrapper, or source checkout that provides this installation.
```

`detectInstallMethod()` is unchanged: every user-facing path already
goes through the ownership check, and returning `unknown` would trip the

Preserve non-floating buffers in ZeRO checkpoint conversion (#8515)

ZeRO checkpoint reconstruction currently converts every persistent
buffer to fp32. This silently changes integer values before
`load_state_dict()` gets a chance to restore their dtype. For example,
an int64 buffer containing `16777217` becomes `16777216`; reloading a
small model that uses those offsets changes its output from `3.98585796`
to `1.99292898`. The newer dtype-selectable exporter also casts all
buffers while planning and materializing shards, so fixing
reconstruction alone is insufficient.

Restrict precision conversion to floating-point tensors. Integer,
boolean, and other non-floating buffers retain their dtype and values
during reconstruction and export, while floating buffers still recover
to fp32 and follow the requested export dtype. The same dtype selection
is used for empty shard-planning tensors and materialized output,
keeping shard sizes accurate. Shared tensor aliases remain preserved.

The regression tests save actual ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 checkpoints after a
small SGD training step, reconstruct and export them, reload the model,
and compare its output. They cover int64 offsets above the fp32
exact-integer range, boolean masks, fp16 source buffers, fp32/fp16/bf16
exports, and sharded-file metadata. The expected precision-converted
model comes from PyTorch's `Module.to(dtype).float()` behavior.

The existing conversion integration test also now uses `tmp_path`: its
previous `tmpdir` object returned a legacy `py.path` stat wrapper that
raises `AttributeError: st_st_size` at the existing `.stat().st_size`

title: Fix TapGestureRecognizer stuck state when native dialog swallows pointer events
body:
Fix TapGestureRecognizer stuck state when native dialog swallows pointer events

## Background

On Windows, when a native platform dialog (e.g. file picker opened via `IFileDialog` / `file_selector` package) closes after the user **confirms** (clicks "Open" / "Save"), the OS may have swallowed the pointer up/cancel events that originated from the Flutter window before the dialog appeared.

**Why clicking X to dismiss works but confirming doesn't:**
- Clicking X → dialog sends a close event → Windows forwards the pointer up back to the original window → Flutter receives it → TapGestureRecognizer completes normally → `_reset()` called → `state = ready`
- Clicking "Open" → dialog closes via native file operation → pointer events consumed by OS → Flutter window never receives pointer up/cancel → TapGestureRecognizer stuck

## Root Cause

`TapGestureRecognizer.addAllowedPointer` guards initialization with:

```dart
if (state == GestureRecognizerState.ready) {
  if (_down != null && _up != null) {
    _reset();  // Only resets when BOTH down AND up have arrived
  }
  _down = event;
}
```

When the native dialog swallowed the up event, the recognizer state is:
- `state` = `possible` (not `ready` — because arena was never resolved)
- `_down` = PointerDownEvent (pointer id = 4)
- `_up` = `null` (swallowed)
- `primaryPointer` = 4

A new user click produces pointer id 74:
1. `addAllowedPointer(74)` → `state != ready` → skip initialization → `_down` stays pointer 4
2. `acceptGesture(74)` → `74 != primaryPointer(4)` → `_checkDown()` / `_checkUp()` never fire → tap never triggers

The widget keeps receiving pointer events (hit test, listener callbacks), but the gesture recognizer state machine is permanently wedged until the widget tree is rebuilt.

## Fix

At the **top** of `addAllowedPointer`, detect the stale sequence and force-resolve it:

```dart
if (state != GestureRecognizerState.ready &&
    _down != null &&
    _down!.pointer != event.pointer) {
  resolve(GestureDisposition.rejected);
  stopTrackingPointer(_down!.pointer);
  _reset();
}
```

The normal guarded block runs afterward — `_reset()` sets `state = ready`, so the existing path handles the new pointer correctly.

### Why this is safe (no behavioral change in normal flows)

The fix only fires when **all three** conditions hold simultaneously:
1. `state != ready` — recognizer is in the middle of tracking a gesture
2. `_down != null` — a previous pointer down was recorded
3. `_down.pointer != event.pointer` — the new pointer id differs from the one being tracked

In normal gesture flows:
- Same pointer down → `_down.pointer == event.pointer` → condition 3 false → **skip**
- Same pointer up → `state` becomes `ready` after arena resolve → condition 1 false → **skip**
- Fresh gesture (all null) → `state == ready` → condition 1 false → **skip**

## Reproduction

```dart
import 'package:file_selector/file_selector.dart';

// After this, TapGestureRecognizer on the TextField/EditableText
// beneath will be stuck — click on it and the cursor won't move.
XFile? file = await openFile();
```

Tested on: Windows 11, Flutter 3.27+, file_selector 1.0+.

## Scope

- `TapGestureRecognizer` (this fix) — **Fixed**
- `DoubleTapGestureRecognizer` — Internally delegates to `TapGestureRecognizer` for the first tap, so it benefits from this fix automatically
- `PanGestureRecognizer` / `DragGestureRecognizer` / `ScaleGestureRecognizer` — Unrelated, OneSequenceGestureRecognizer has its own lifecycle handling
- Desktop only? — iOS `UIImagePickerController` / Android `Activity` intent-based pickers also involve native view transitions that can swallow pointers. Same stale-state class of bug could affect them, but only Windows has been confirmed to trigger it so far.

title: reverseproxy: replace only known placeholders in health check body
body:
Fixes #7021. Implements @mholt's suggestion in that thread ("We could probably switch to replacing only known placeholders"), scoped to the body.

### Problem

The active health check body is expanded with `repl.ReplaceAll`, which blanks any `{...}` the replacer doesn't recognise. Only globals are available here, so a JSON `health_request_body` is sent as an **empty body**:

```
reverse_proxy 10.0.0.2:80 {
	health_request_body `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]}`
}
```

The header values three lines below already use `ReplaceKnown`, so the two halves of the same request were built with different rules.

This isn't limited to bodies without placeholders. A body that **does** use one is mangled too — `{"token":"{env.SOME_VAR}"}` goes out as `"}`, because the opening `{"token":"` is consumed as an unrecognised placeholder before the real one is reached. Both are in the tests.

### Fix

One line: `ReplaceAll` → `ReplaceKnown` for the body. Unrecognised braces are left intact; real placeholders still expand.

### Scope: why the `Host` header is deliberately left alone

I said on the issue that I'd change `Host` on line 454 too, since it uses `ReplaceAll` while the header values below it use `ReplaceKnown`. Testing showed that would make it worse, so I didn't.

Go's HTTP server blanks a `Host` containing braces — sending `Host: {not.a.placeholder}` to an `httptest` server, the handler sees `r.Host == ""`. That's stdlib behaviour. So today `ReplaceAll` blanks an unknown placeholder and Go falls back to the URL host and the request works; `ReplaceKnown` would leave the literal `{...}` in `req.Host` and the upstream would discard it. Happy to revisit if you read it differently.

### Tests

Two cases in `active_health_test.go`, built on the existing `newActiveHandler`/`runActiveHealthCheck` harness:

- a JSON body arrives intact
- a body containing `{env.…}` still has the placeholder expanded

Both fail on `master` and pass with the change:

```
--- FAIL: TestActiveHealthCheckBodyKeepsUnknownPlaceholders
    health check body = "", want "{\"jsonrpc\":\"2.0\",...}"
--- FAIL: TestActiveHealthCheckBodyStillReplacesKnownPlaceholders
    health check body = "\"}", want "{\"token\":\"s3cret\"}"
```

`go test ./modules/caddyhttp/...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

### Disclosure

Per CONTRIBUTING: this was written with AI assistance (Claude). I can explain every line, and the behaviour of both the fix and the `Host` finding above was verified by running the tests, not inferred.

title: dbeaver/dbeaver#42524 Use zero-based index in JDBCResultSetCallable.getAttributeValue
body:
Closes dbeaver/dbeaver#42524

### Problem
`DBCResultSet.getAttributeValue(int index)` is zero-based (see its Javadoc, and `JDBCResultSetImpl`, which calls `getObject(index + 1)`). `JDBCResultSetCallable`, the result set built from procedure OUT parameters, passed the index to its own 1-based `getObject(int)` unchanged:
- index 0 -> `IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index -1 out of bounds`
- index N -> value of column N-1

The SQL editor result viewer is not affected because value handlers read JDBC result sets with 1-based indexes. Generic zero-based callers are, e.g. `SQLScriptDataReceiver` when an SQL Script task dumps query results to the log.

### Change
- `JDBCResultSetCallable.getAttributeValue(int)`: `getObject(index)` -> `getObject(index + 1)`.
- No callers compensate for the old behaviour (checked for `getAttributeValue(... + 1)` and other special handling of `JDBCResultSetCallable`).

### Tests
- New `JDBCResultSetCallableTest`: a `CALL` with two OUT parameters, checks that attribute indexes 0 and 1 return the first and second values. Passes with the change; the same scenario run against the unchanged bundle reproduces the failure (index 0 -> `IndexOutOfBoundsException`, index 1 -> `first`).

### Manual test in DBeaver
Built DBeaver CE (Windows, JDK 25) with and without this change. HSQLDB 2.7.4 embedded, procedure `GET_TWO(OUT A, OUT B)` returning `'first'`, `'second'`; SQL Script task running `CALL GET_TWO(?, ?);` with **Dump query results to log file** enabled:
- Before: the task fails with `IndexOutOfBoundsException: Index -1 out of bounds for length 2` at `JDBCResultSetCallable.getAttributeValue(JDBCResultSetCallable.java:69)` <- `SQLScriptDataReceiver.fetchRow`.
- After: the task finishes successfully and the log contains `first	second`.

title: fix(proxy): verify runtime links before showing a connected chain
body:
## Problem

The proxy-chain page can show Disconnect while the displayed chain is not applied. For example, select `exit` in a proxy group, then arrange `entry -> exit` without connecting it: the existing predicate accepts the selected exit even when `exit` has no `dialer-proxy`. A cached exit name can also report a connection after the runtime links disappear, or after changing the entry while keeping the same exit.

This addresses the misleading connected state associated with #6646 and #7012. It does not resolve the separate lifecycle problem that removes runtime chains; #7856 proposes preserving them across profile refreshes.

## Approach

Require both the selected exit and every adjacent `dialer-proxy` relationship to match the displayed chain in the runtime configuration. Use the runtime-config query already loaded by the page, and refresh it alongside proxy selections after connecting or disconnecting. Cached exit metadata is no longer evidence that a chain is connected.

Two focused regression tests cover losing the runtime links while the exit stays selected, and editing an entry or intermediate hop while retaining the exit. Valid two-hop and three-hop chains remain connected. These cases distinguish an applied chain from the selection-only condition that caused the false positive.

## Scope

Changes are limited to the chain status predicate, its refresh points, and its regression tests. This checks applied configuration, not node reachability, and adds no persistence or dependency changes.

message:
coverage: Let `@path` use plain images without code from the tracked path (#63564)

Since #62724, every coverage request needs instrumented package images, so
`--code-coverage=@path` (the `julia-runtest` default) precompiles every
standard library it loads into the user depot, because the bundled images
carry no counters. Frequent nightly updates keep invalidating such caches.

A path request only reports files under the tracked path, so a plain image
without code from there serves it equally well. Deciding that does not
require scanning debug information: an image only contains code from its own
source files, from the images it was built against, and from the system
image (code that names other files, e.g. through `include_string`, is not
detected). The loader therefore accepts a plain image when none of the
package's source files are tracked and every already-loaded package
dependency was accepted the same way. Dependencies that still have to be
loaded go through the same check, and because the image pins their build
ids, a tracked dependency that must load instrumented forces its dependents
to be rebuilt. The system image's recorded sources must not overlap the
tracked path, and the system image itself must be plain, since otherwise
plain images can have been built against instrumented dependencies.

The runtime keeps a registry of the plain images the loader accepted: only
those pass validation under a coverage request, and their code is kept
rather than reinferred.

`Pkg.test` precompiles from a parent process that collects no coverage
itself, so the requested tracked path travels in `CacheFlags`, outside the
image's identity: the driver judges caches for that path instead of its own
options, and its workers inherit it so that they accept the same
dependencies. Only a process collecting that very request records accepted
images for the runtime.

Adds an APIVerve bundle to `lfx-bundles`, backed by APIVerve's HTTP API.

[APIVerve](https://apiverve.com) is a catalog of about 380 REST APIs behind one key: email and phone validation, IP geolocation, DNS, WHOIS and SSL lookups, exchange rates, stock and SEC data, VIN decoding, PDF and screenshot generation, and more.

title: Fix keys of an interposed Seq iterated in reverse
body:
`interpose` numbers its keys in iteration order, so when it is iterated in reverse the last value gets key 0:

```js
Seq([1, 2, 3]).interpose(0).lastIndexOf(1); // 4, expected 0
Seq([1, 2, 3]).interpose(0).findLastIndex((x) => x === 3); // 0, expected 4
```

`List#interpose` is fine because the List is built in a forward pass, but a lazy Seq (including `Range`) hits it through `lastIndexOf`, `findLastIndex`, `findLastEntry`, `reduceRight` and reversed iterators.

It's the same problem as #2309 (filter), in `interposeFactory`. In reverse, keys now count down from the size of the interposed sequence. When that size is unknown (e.g. after `filter`), `ensureSize` works it out first, like #2309 does.

The new test in `__tests__/interpose.ts` covers a Seq of known and unknown size, through both `__iterate` and `__iterator`. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. The same code is on `6.x`.

I used Claude Code to write this change.

title: feat(dashboard): opt-in quota window and expiring reset credit alerts
body:
## What

Opt-in dashboard alerts for two ways quota silently disappears:

1. **A usage window drops low** — one toast when a window crosses **35 % remaining** (warning) or **15 %** (critical), per connection per window.
2. **A banked reset credit is about to expire** — one toast when a credit enters its last **24 h**, so it can be spent instead of wasted.

Both are computed **client-side from the snapshot the dashboard already polls** (cache-only, every 5 min). No new endpoint calls upstream, no request is made to the provider, and **no reset credit is consumed** — this PR only observes and notifies.

## Why

PR #18630 makes expiring credits auto-spend themselves, but it is a server scheduler: it only helps connections the operator opted in there. A credit that expires while the dashboard is open and nothing else is watching still disappears without a word. These alerts close that last gap with zero new server load.

## Design

- **`quotaWindowAlerts.ts`** — pure functions, no React, no store: `collectQuotaWindowAlerts` and `collectResetCreditExpiryAlerts`. Every branch is unit-testable.
- **Edge-triggered, not level-triggered.** A window sitting at 3 % for six hours produces **one** toast, not one per poll. The `latch` clears when the window recovers, so a later drop alerts again.
- **Dedupe survives a reload** — the latch is persisted in `key_value` (namespace `quotaAlertLatch`), so refreshing the page does not re-toast everything. **No migration.**
- **Opt-in, default OFF** — new `codexQuotaAlerts.enabled` setting (default `false` in `src/lib/db/settings.ts` + Zod schema). A failed/slow `/api/settings` read leaves alerts off rather than guessing.
- **Ignored rows:** credit balances (`isResetCredits`/`isCredits`), unlimited buckets, windows already past their reset (`staleAfterReset` — `quotaParsing` zeroes those, alerting would page the operator about a window that just rolled over), and any row without a real `remainingPercentage`.
- **Manual redemption is untouched.** The card selection, `selectionToken`, FEFO ordering and idempotency key are exactly as they are today; this PR adds no button and changes no click path.

Existing infra reused: `notificationStore` toasts (`notify.warning` / `notify.error`), `fetchWithTimeout`.

## Bugs the tests caught (fixed here)

- **`Number(null) === 0`** in `getQuotaAlertLatch`: a corrupted `null` latch value was resurrected as a real threshold of `0`, which would have suppressed or mis-fired an alert. Now only genuine numbers are accepted.

## Tests

All failing-first (TDD): the 15 evaluator tests failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` before the module existed; the DB tests failed with the `Number(null)` bug above.

```
tests/unit/codex-quota-window-alerts.test.ts           15/15
tests/unit/quota-alert-latch.test.ts                    6/6
tests/unit/codex-quota-alerts-settings-schema.test.ts   5/5
                                                       25/25
```

Coverage of the spec: ① threshold crossed → alert once · ② expiring credit → reminder · ③ disabled → silent · ④ recovery re-arms · ⑤ separate latches per connection/window · ⑥ credit rows, unlimited, stale-after-reset and percentage-less rows ignored · ⑦ persistence round-trip, overwrite, corrupt row, clear.

Gates:
- `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --pretty false -p tsconfig.typecheck-core.json` → **exit 0, 0 lines**
- `check-key-completeness.mjs` → **OK — 66 locales carry all 14585 keys**
- `check-ui-keys-coverage.mjs` → **PASS — 66 locales at or above 80 %**
- `check-ui-icu.mjs` → **PASS — all 977195 messages in 67 catalogs compile**

## i18n

3 new keys (`quotaAlertTitle`, `quotaAlertWindowLow`, `quotaAlertCreditExpiring`) added to **all 67 catalogs** via `scripts/ad-hoc/insert-quota-alert-i18n-keys.py`. The script is **insert-only**: it splices 3 lines after `resetCreditNoExpiry` and re-parses the file to guarantee valid JSON — no reordering, no reformatting (`67 files changed, 201 insertions(+)`, 0 deletions).

## Scope guard

Display/notification only. No scheduler, no SSE, no new provider call, no change to credit selection or redemption. Combos are untouched.

title: fix(fill): set value-type inputs directly and refuse elements that can't take text
body:
Fixes #2055. Fixes #2000.

`fill` and `type` focused the element and sent `Input.insertText` without checking that it takes text. Chrome drops inserted text on date and time inputs, so `fill` left them empty and printed `✓ Done` (#2000). On a select, checkbox, button, color, range or disabled input, the text went into whichever field last had focus (#2055).

## Change

- `fill` focuses color, date, time, datetime-local, month, range and week inputs, sets the value with the native value setter and fires `input` and `change`, as Playwright's `fill` does. A value the input rejects fails with the format it expects (`YYYY-MM-DD`) and leaves the field as it was.
- `fill` and `type` refuse selects and buttons (unless contenteditable), non-text inputs (checkbox, radio, file and so on) and disabled fields before touching anything, e.g. `Input of type "checkbox" cannot be filled`. `type` on a date or color input points to `fill`.
- A label stands for its control unless it is editable itself, as in Playwright, so `fill` on a label for a date input sets the date. A snapshot ref for a date or time input points at its month, day or hour field, which stands for the input too, so `fill @e4 2024-05-06` works.
- Other elements are focused and typed into as before.
- `--help`, README, the core skill, the docs commands page and the MCP descriptions are updated.

Not covered: a focusable element that isn't a form control, such as a `div[role=combobox]`, still takes the old path. Checking where focus lands instead broke rich-text editors, Monaco, Vue's `nextTick`, inline editors and UI5's async `focus()`, so that is left for a separate change. Readonly fields are left to #1921, which edits the same focus call; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Tests

A new e2e test covers each row of #2055's table, #2000's repro, malformed values, labels, a date input filled through its snapshot ref, contenteditable labels and buttons, and a focus handler that re-renders the field. It checks that a refusal leaves the previously focused field alone. The issue rows fail on main. Ran on Linux with Chromium 141:

- `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test`: 1,440 passed; `test_get_socket_dir_home_fallback` fails the same way on main when run as root
- e2e: the new test, `e2e_form_interaction`, `e2e_error_handling`, both `e2e_select_option_*` and `e2e_material_checkbox_check_uncheck`
- docs: `test`, `type-check`, `build` and `test:routes`

title: [JsonPath] Accumulate recursive traversal results in one array
body:
| Q             | A
| ------------- | ---
| Branch?       | 8.2
| Bug fix?      | no
| New feature?  | no
| Deprecations? | no
| Issues        | None
| License       | MIT

`JsonCrawler::evaluateRecursive()` creates a result array for every recursive call, then copies the accumulated prefix into another array with `array_merge()` for each child. Wide JSON trees repeatedly copy the same node references.

Pass the result array by reference through recursive calls and append each visited container directly. The initial invocation gets a fresh empty array; recursive invocations share it. Traversal keeps the same depth-first order and includes the same arrays and objects. Recursion depth handling and the returned node list stay the same.

The new tests cover traversal across sibling nodes, ordinary and quoted recursive selectors, duplicate values, `null`, `false`, missing properties, and repeated calls. They also verify that independent recursive invocations do not share results. For example, `$[*]..id` on `[{"id":0,"children":[{"id":null}]},{"id":false,"children":[{"id":0}]}]` still returns `[0, null, false, 0]` on every call.

Only a private method signature changes. This adds no public API, options, caching or input restrictions. The separate token result aggregation optimization is not included in this diff or its measurements.

**Validation**

- Non-compliance component tests: 307 tests, 601 assertions, passing.
- Full component suite, including the pinned external compliance dataset: 1472 tests, 1766 assertions, 50 failures on both the unmodified base and this PR. Every individual testcase has the same pass/fail outcome and failure type/message in the JUnit reports. There are no skips or new failures.
- The other optimization applied together with this one: the same full-suite outcomes. Both source files and the tests merge without conflicts. The merged `JsonCrawlerTest` passes all 186 cases and 306 assertions.
- Memory probes on 55 scalar, empty and small-input/query pairs, plus all 5000 generated cases: no increase in the PHP-managed peak for either independent change.
- Differential checks against the base: 200 generated JSON documents with 25 queries each, including recursive selectors, duplicate selectors, filters, scalar/null inputs and invalid selectors. All 5000 results or exception class/message pairs match for each independent change and their combination.
- PHP CS Fixer with the repository configuration: both changed files clean. `git diff --check`: clean.

The new compatibility tests also pass on the base source. They protect existing behavior; the timings below demonstrate the performance improvement. No timing threshold is added to the test suite.

The 50 existing failures are invalid name selectors containing unescaped control characters, with both single and double quotes. They cover U+0000 through U+0007, U+000E through U+001B, and U+001D through U+001F, once per quote style. Their error is:

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the time and memory measurements</summary>

Save the two scripts below together as `worker.php` and `run.py`. From a checkout of this PR with dependencies installed, run:

```sh
git show 2e82606203583acf71e73bd8cf84dd3d0216aa3b:src/Symfony/Component/JsonPath/JsonCrawler.php > /tmp/JsonCrawler.before.php
python3 run.py "$PWD" /tmp/JsonCrawler.before.php "$PWD/src/Symfony/Component/JsonPath/JsonCrawler.php" > results.json
```

`results.json` contains every raw time and memory sample, plus a digest of each result. The driver verifies that matching before/after cases produce the same digest. It requires Python 3 and PHP with `memory_reset_peak_usage()`, available as `php` on PATH.

`worker.php`:

```php
<?php
// Usage: php worker.php /path/to/symfony /path/to/JsonCrawler.php
[$script, $root, $source] = $argv;
$loader = require $root.'/vendor/autoload.php';
$loader->addPsr4('Symfony\\Component\\JsonPath\\', $root.'/src/Symfony/Component/JsonPath', true);
require $source;
foreach ([10 => 1000, 100 => 100, 1000 => 20, 5000 => 3] as $size => $iterations) {
    $data = [];
    for ($i = 0; $i < $size; ++$i) {
        $data[] = ['id' => $i, 'nested' => ['name' => 'item'.$i, 'values' => [1, null, false, 0]]];
    }
    $crawler = new Symfony\Component\JsonPath\JsonCrawler(json_encode($data));
    foreach (['$[*].id', '$..id'] as $query) {
        for ($j = 0; $j < 2; ++$j) {
            $result = $crawler->find($query);
            unset($result);
        }
        memory_reset_peak_usage();
        $used = memory_get_usage(false);
        $allocated = memory_get_usage(true);
        $result = $crawler->find($query);
        $peak = memory_get_peak_usage(false) - $used;
        $allocatorPeak = memory_get_peak_usage(true) - $allocated;
        $retained = memory_get_usage(false) - $used;
        $digest = hash('sha256', serialize($result));
        unset($result);
        $start = hrtime(true);
        for ($j = 0; $j < $iterations; ++$j) {
            $result = $crawler->find($query);
            unset($result);
        }
        $elapsed = (hrtime(true) - $start) / 1e6;
        echo json_encode(['size' => $size, 'query' => $query, 'iterations' => $iterations, 'ms' => $elapsed, 'peak_bytes' => $peak, 'retained_bytes' => $retained, 'allocator_peak_bytes' => $allocatorPeak, 'digest' => $digest]), "\n";
    }
}
```

`run.py`:

```python
import json
import pathlib
import subprocess
import sys

root, before, after = sys.argv[1:]
worker = str(pathlib.Path(__file__).with_name('worker.php'))
results = []
for opcache in (0, 1):
    for round in range(9):
        for variant in (('before', 'after') if round % 2 == 0 else ('after', 'before')):
            source = before if variant == 'before' else after
            output = subprocess.check_output([
                'php', '-d', f'opcache.enable_cli={opcache}',
                '-d', 'opcache.jit=disable', '-d', 'opcache.file_update_protection=0',
                worker, root, source,
            ], text=True)
            for line in output.splitlines():
                results.append(dict(json.loads(line), opcache=opcache, round=round, variant=variant))
for opcache in (0, 1):
    for round in range(9):
        pair = [[r for r in results if r['opcache'] == opcache and r['round'] == round and r['variant'] == variant] for variant in ('before', 'after')]
        assert [(r['size'], r['query'], r['digest']) for r in pair[0]] == [(r['size'], r['query'], r['digest']) for r in pair[1]]
print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
```

</details>

<details>

gh api 'repos/jsonpath-standard/jsonpath-compliance-test-suite/contents/cts.json?ref=9d1a415a53f5dfb291bc874823892e49174e38eb' -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github.raw+json' > vendor/jsonpath-standard/jsonpath-compliance-test-suite/cts.json

$loader = require $root.'/vendor/autoload.php';

title: feat(cua-driver): add JPEG screenshots to get_window_state and encode from raw pixels
body:
## Summary

`get_window_state` on macOS encoded every capture as PNG, and when the window was larger than the `max_image_dimension` ceiling (1366 by default) it decoded that PNG again, resized it with Lanczos3 and re-encoded it.

This keeps the raw RGBA pixels from ScreenCaptureKit and the SkyLight off-Space capture (new `CapturedImage` / `RgbaFrame` in `cua_driver_core::image_utils`), so the screenshot is resized and encoded once. The `screencapture` shell fallback still hands back a PNG and goes through the old path. `screenshot_window_bytes` keeps its signature and output for every other caller.

It also adds two optional `get_window_state` arguments on macOS:

- `screenshot_format`: `"png"` (default) or `"jpeg"`.
- `screenshot_quality`: JPEG quality 1–95, default 85; refused unless `screenshot_format` is `"jpeg"`.

The values and range mirror the existing `screenshot` tool's `format`/`quality`; the `screenshot_` prefix matches `include_screenshot` and `screenshot_out_file` and keeps them apart from `tree_format`. A JPEG read sets `screenshot_mime_type: "image/jpeg"`, sends an `image/jpeg` image part (or writes JPEG to `screenshot_out_file`), drops alpha, keeps the same dimensions and pixel-to-window mapping, and mints no `capture_id`, because the capture registry stores and validates PNG captures only.

Scope and limits:

- Default output is byte-identical: PNG is lossless, so resizing the raw pixels gives the same image as resizing the decoded PNG, and both go through the same encoder. A unit test checks this for several caps, and live reads of Calculator (230×408, not resized) and a TextEdit document (768×1569, resized to 669×1366) returned the same SHA-256 as main.
- `get_desktop_state` and `zoom` are unchanged: `zoom` already returns JPEG, and the desktop PNG is the coordinate source behind its mandatory `capture_id`.
- Linux and Windows do not advertise the new arguments, so the registry refuses them there as unknown arguments. The portable contract manifest is a subset and does not list them; `cua-contract-gen all --check` is unaffected.

## Numbers

Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.3.1, on the external 1× display. In-process timings of the encode step on real captures (median of 30, release build):

| window (raw capture) | main path | this PR, PNG | this PR, JPEG q85 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Calculator 230×408 (no resize) | 0.5 ms | 0.4 ms | 1.0 ms |
| TextEdit 768×1569 → 669×1366 | 25.3 ms | 23.4 ms | 29.0 ms |

Breakdown for the TextEdit capture: the Lanczos3 resize is 23 ms of it at 1× and 72 ms when the same content is doubled to a Retina-sized 1536×3138 frame, while the PNG round trip this PR removes is about 2 ms at 1× and about 7 ms at 2× (full-size encode plus decode). So the default-path saving is small for flat UI content and grows with capture size and entropy; the resize dominates and is untouched here.

Image size, same reads:

| window | PNG | JPEG q85 |
|---|---|---|
| Calculator | 46,524 B | 22,127 B (−52%) |
| TextEdit document | 44,380 B | 36,536 B (−18%) |

For flat UI captures like these, the `image` crate's JPEG encoder is slower than its PNG encoder (6.5 ms vs 0.8 ms on the resized TextEdit frame), so `"jpeg"` trades a few milliseconds for a smaller payload; it does not make the read faster. End to end through the daemon (`cua-driver serve` plus `cua-driver mcp --socket`, 15 reads, two rounds), `get_window_state` tree+shot medians were 211–384 ms on main, 249–421 ms for this PR's PNG and 233–297 ms for JPEG on the two windows, with p90 up to 700 ms: the machine was shared with other builds (load average 35–50), so those numbers do not resolve differences of a few milliseconds either way.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p cua-driver-core --lib`: 1083 passed, 1 ignored. New tests: PNG from raw pixels is byte-identical to the PNG round trip for caps 0, 300, 1366, 120 and 77; JPEG from raw pixels and from PNG keeps the resized dimensions and decodes; `ScreenshotEncoding::from_args` defaults, bounds and refusals.
- `cargo test -p platform-macos --lib`: 636 passed, 7 ignored (capture backend and prefetch tests updated for the generic capture type).
- `cargo fmt --all --check` passes. `cargo clippy -p cua-driver-core --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes. `cargo clippy -p platform-macos --all-targets`: no findings in the changed files; the same 5 findings as main in files this PR does not touch (`ax/reveal_scroll.rs:185`, `tools/click.rs:153` ×3, `document_edit.rs:65`).
- Live on macOS with a release build: default reads byte-identical to main (above); JPEG reads return `image/jpeg`, the same dimensions and no `capture_id`.
- Docs: regenerated `docs/content/docs/cua-driver/reference/mcp-tools` and the macOS snapshot with `scripts/docs-generators/cua-driver.ts` from a native dump (`--check` passes).
- All Rust checks ran from a private target directory for this worktree.
- Not run: Linux and Windows builds (no code there changed beyond the shared `image_utils` additions) and the desktop E2E matrix.

title: fix(ssh): let sshpass and other terminal drivers answer ssh prompts
body:
Running `sshpass -p '...' ssh host` from Crush's shell ignored the password and fell back to Crush's password dialog, so sign-in failed with "Permission denied". Crush forces OpenSSH to send every credential prompt to its askpass helper, which hid the prompt from tools like `sshpass` and `expect` that answer by watching ssh's terminal.

- Crush starts every shell command without a terminal, so if ssh has one, a driver such as `sshpass` set it up on purpose. The askpass helper now asks on that terminal, the way ssh would by itself, so the driver's explicit password goes through. Commands without a terminal still get the native dialog, and security key touch notices always show in the UI.
- Tests use real pseudo-terminals to stand in for `sshpass`, and the change was checked by hand against the real `sshpass`.
